Israel election: People protest across cities calling for Jewish-Arab govt Demonstrations in Jerusalem, Tel Aviv and Haifa called for inclusive governance, while partial results showed the pro-Netanyahu bloc leading with 53 seats against 48 for the opposing bloc

Protesters sit on a road as they take part in a rally demanding that Israel-Arab parties in Israel be included in the formation of the next government coalition | Image: Reuters

ANI 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 29 2026 | 7:55 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Around 300 individuals have assembled to protest at Paris Square in Jerusalem, Mesila Park in Tel Aviv and UNESCO Square in Haifa, advocating for the establishment of a Jewish-Arab government, according to the Israeli daily newspaper Haaretz. Demonstrators brandished placards featuring slogans such as "Freedom for all, from the river to the sea" and "Yes to a Jewish-Arab government". The demonstrations reflect a unified call among the protest participants for inclusive governance, as reported by Haaretz. Against this backdrop of civil demonstrations, vote counting progresses in Israel's high-stakes political contest, where partial returns published by the Central Elections Committee and detailed by The Times of Israel indicate that the electoral arithmetic remains finely balanced as the night unfolds.

According to partial figures published by the Central Elections Committee as of 11:35 pm (local time), the pro-Netanyahu bloc holds 53 seats, while the opposing bloc stands at 48 seats, based on 90 per cent of votes counted across 97.5 per cent of ballot boxes. Also Read

The updated tallies also shed light on several political factions currently tracking beneath the 3.25 per cent electoral threshold. Parties hovering below the cutoff include the Reservists at 2.6 per cent, the People of Israel at 1.6 per cent and the Charedi Public faction at 0.2 per cent. Electoral authorities have emphasised that these returns are strictly partial and will continue to evolve as the count advances. According to The Times of Israel, votes cast in double envelopes, which notably include the ballots of active-duty soldiers, are traditionally processed in the later stages of tabulation, leaving the final parliamentary breakdown subject to change.

Reflecting on these unfolding numbers, Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot, the leading opposition candidate, stated that the election results constitute a clear vote of no confidence in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's administration, pledging to press ahead with efforts to oust the government even though his political bloc remains well short of a parliamentary majority. "This is the will of the people, who expressed no confidence in the government of October 7 and draft evasion, and in the draft-dodgers' bloc as a whole," Eisenkot wrote on X, taking direct aim at Netanyahu and his political allies. While pro-Netanyahu parties control 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats, his opponents hold 67. However, that opposing faction remains divided between Jewish-led parties commanding 48 seats and Arab-led parties holding 19, with the majority of Jewish-led factions expressing unwillingness to form partnerships with Arab-led groups.

"We have more long days of work ahead of us, but we are focused on the weighty task entrusted to us: bringing change to Israel and establishing a Zionist government committed to military conscription," Eisenkot added, following what he described as a long day of meetings, vowing to "rise to the great challenge ahead of us". Amid these ongoing political developments, Yair Golan, chairman of the left-wing political faction The Democrats, marked his first media interaction since election polls closed by announcing that he intends to meet with three distinct party leaders for talks aimed at government formation, though he withheld their specific identities.

Golan's upcoming political engagements encompass key opposition figures, including Yashar party chief Gadi Eisenkot, alongside B'Yachad deputy leader Yair Lapid, as reported by The Times of Israel. As a member of a four-party grouping comprising Zionist opposition factions, Golan stands apart as the sole leader within his alliance who has openly endorsed the prospect of integrating Arab parties into a coalition. In an interview with Channel 12, Golan remarked, "I hope to meet with all of them by Sunday." When pressed by the broadcaster on whether Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman formed part of his Thursday itinerary, Golan opted against disclosing names, according to The Times of Israel.

Outlining his political strategy, Golan emphasised his commitment to persuading fellow opposition leaders that they share a unified cause, stating that they are bound by "an overarching mission: to bring hope to the people of Israel". Furthermore, Golan stressed that establishing a new administration is vital to effectively managing pressing security challenges, halting the incumbent government's controversial judicial overhaul and revitalising hope among the younger demographic, who are currently "asking whether they even want to live in this country".

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

Nike deepens India push with new running shoe, Vegam Run, at ₹3,795 The sportswear giant will release the shoe on Flipkart on November 1, as it seeks to tap India's running boom and revive growth amid sales weakness in key markets, including China

Nike's Vegam Run | Image: Company website

Reuters NEW YORK 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 29 2026 | 7:36 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Nike unveiled on Wednesday its first-ever running shoe designed specifically for India, marking the sportswear giant's latest bid to reach shoppers in the world's most populous country as it grapples with a sales slump in other key regions including China. The shoe, dubbed Vegam Run, follows Nike's announcement earlier this month that it plans to open a new campus in India, where it is seeking to make inroads amid a running boom. The running shoe is set to be released on India's e-commerce marketplace Flipkart on November 1, priced at ₹3,795 (roughly $40). It was developed in about five months, Nike said.

CEO Elliott Hill, two years into his tenure, is betting on a revamped product pipeline to turn around the struggling sportswear juggernaut, which analysts say will hinge in large part on locally led designs in key markets. Nike is trying to push into India at a time when China, historically a profit driver for the company, continues to show particular weakness. Sales in China, which account for about 15 per cent of Nike's annual revenue, have fallen for nine consecutive quarters as international rivals and domestic sportswear groups gain traction. Shares have tumbled more than 40 per cent so far this year. But Nike's global running business has emerged as a bright spot, growing by double digits for six consecutive quarters.

"Our Nike performance business is not yet large enough to offset the pressure we're seeing in Nike sportswear, Jordan brand, and Greater China," Hill warned analysts this month after the company projected a surprisingly steep drop in full-year revenue.

item.title: JPMorgan to lead US retail offering in Anthropic's potential record IPO
item.description: The company behind Claude has weighed a retail offering of about 15% to 20% of the shares available in the IPO overall ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Ryan Gould and Shirin Ghaffary Anthropic PBC has tapped JPMorgan Chase & Co. to lead US sales of shares to individual investors in its potentially record-setting initial public offering, people familiar with the matter said. The company behind Claude has weighed a retail offering of about 15% to 20% of the shares available in the IPO overall, some of the people said. JPMorgan Chief Executive Officer Jamie Dimon is expected to take part in the Wall Street bank’s campaign, one of them added. JPMorgan is reprising its role leading the effort to gather retail orders for SpaceX’s $86.2 billion IPO, which saw more than $100 billion of demand from individual investors, Bloomberg News has reported.  Citigroup Inc. is set to coordinate the international retail offering, some of the people said, asking not to be identified as the information isn’t public. Anthropic’s IPO includes offerings in Australia, Canada, Japan, certain European Economic Area countries, Switzerland and the UK, according to the IPO filing. JPMorgan is coordinating outreach on Anthropic’s IPO to high-net-worth investors and private banking clients as well as broker platforms, the people said. Deliberations are ongoing and details including the share of the offering earmarked for retail could change, the people said. Representatives for Anthropic, JPMorgan and Citigroup declined to comment. Anthropic filed publicly on Monday for an IPO that would see it and some of its investors sell shares, marking the first listing by a company focused primarily on developing the most advanced AI models. Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley are leading the offering. Investors are telling bankers on the deal that their estimate of a fair valuation has shifted to around $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion, though a valuation of closer to $1.75 trillion is potentially achievable, Bloomberg News has reported. The amount of money needed to fund the development of AI and its associated infrastructure has spurred companies to raise tens of billions of dollars at a time.  Meta Platforms Inc. on Monday kicked off a plan to raise as much as $98 billion in equity, which would be one of the largest financing exercises of its kind in history. It follows Google parent Alphabet Inc.’s $85 billion equity fundraising plan earlier this year. Anthropic and rival OpenAI are seeking to raise record amounts while facing mounting public scrutiny over AI safety after a string of high-profile hacking incidents by rogue agents.

item.title: Microsoft India offers voluntary exit with 1 month salary per yr of service
item.description: Eligible employees selected for the programme must decide by December 1, with the package also including health insurance and career transition services ...
item.dc:creator: Aashish Aryan
item.content:encoded: Microsoft will offer employees in India a standard severance package, including one month of base salary for each completed year of service, health insurance and career transition services, as part of its voluntary retirement programme, the company said. Microsoft India employees selected for the voluntary retirement scheme must decide by December 1, the company said. While the company did not share details of the number of employees impacted in India, a spokesperson said Microsoft continues to “invest in India’s talent and technology ecosystem and is backing the country’s AI ambitions with $20.5 billion in committed investment between 2025 and 2029 across cloud and AI infrastructure, skilling and operations”. “We are also on track to fulfil our commitment of equipping 20 million people across India with AI skills by 2030,” the spokesperson said. Earlier on Monday, the company offered a voluntary exit scheme to nearly 60,000 employees globally, or roughly 25 per cent of its 223,000-strong workforce. “This offer will be available to eligible employees in participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States at level 70 and below,” said Amy Coleman, executive vice-president and chief people officer at Microsoft. The decision to offer the voluntary retirement programme to roughly one-fourth of its workforce comes as companies worldwide look to improve efficiency and shore up revenues with artificial intelligence, leading to layoffs or retirement programmes such as the one Microsoft is offering. In a blog post, Coleman said the voluntary exit offer was an important part of how Microsoft was “creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter”. The voluntary exit programme comes even as Microsoft continues to hire. In a LinkedIn post on Saturday, Coleman said the company welcomed 1,600 new employees between October 19 and 23. “There’s a lot of conversation about what AI will mean for jobs. Some companies see AI as a reason to hire fewer people early in their careers. At Microsoft, we see it differently. Every leader we’ll need in ten years is starting their career somewhere today. We want them starting here,” Coleman said in the post.
